added_failures_note: The reviewed run's baseline_suite and after_suite are both readable and both passed: logs/base-gate-d7676e478fc8701b036ec717f80d403c3ead86f5.log and logs/head-gate-7ef7424513cb16aab82e15908db6207ced873d22.log each end EXIT=0 with '1 passed', and neither names a failing test id. assertion_audit: The commit adds no assertion; it changes one HTML fragment and three SVGs. The only guard that reaches these paths is tests/test_artifacts_carry_no_worktree_paths.py, whose positive control fails if its candidate enumeration returns nothing it is known to hold, and whose offender assertion reddens if a tracked file names a reckon worktree path; it says nothing about the reported values.

durability.reason: evidence-only node: the write scope is one fragment and a figure directory, with no source or test file, so no assertion can pin the reported numbers; the rows are kept as JSONL receipts under the run directory and the path-hygiene test covers the committed artefacts.

findings.text: The sentence says stored fits are reused "where their arm, noise scale and iteration budget match", but the generator's reuse predicate (study/full_arm.py:36-49) keys only on arm=="main" and a unique realisation index and carries no budget or scale field, so a mismatched earlier run would be mixed into the 32 silently while the record states the check was made.

The after_suite line names revision 7ef7424513cb, which is this review's base, while the reviewed head is ffce4cd56 and the worktree reflog shows HEAD advanced to ffce4cd56 at 13:09:56, so the gate log's revision label names the pre-change tree even though the 13:16 run read the changed one.
